subject: Temporary reviewer provisioning for SOC 2 artifacts and expiring download tokens
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short-lived auditor access + download scope for SOC 2 artifacts

Hi Nikhil,

We have an auditor (Oliver Park, Audit Partners) starting a scoped review next Tuesday. Their procurement team requires a short-lived, auditable way to pull evidence from your trust portal rather than having a sponsored Okta account provisioned in their IdP.

Can Redwood do one of the following?
- Issue a one-time download token (48h max) scoped to a specific evidence bundle, or
- Create a sponsored reviewer account limited to "view + download" for the same 48h window, or
- Provide a signed bridge-letter/attestation for any gap in coverage for Apr–Jun 2026 if an auditor cannot access files older than 90 days.

Requirements from our side:
- Auditor: Oliver Park <oliver.park@auditpartners.com>
- Scope: SOC 2 Type II report (2025-10 to 2026-03) and supplementary evidence folder "ACME_SOC2_EVIDENCE_2026"
- Access: download allowed (we prefer view+download for evidence bundle)
- Security: token must be single-use, IP-restrictable to Audit Partners' egress and expire within 48 hours

Attached is the list of evidence items we expect to pull. Please advise the safest/fastest path and any docs you need from us (POC, attestations, IP ranges).

Thanks — Sara
Sara Chen
Compliance Manager, Acme Health

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-18T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived auditor access + download scope for SOC 2 artifacts

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. We can support both options (one-time download token or sponsored reviewer) with a couple of controls. Quick questions so I scope this correctly:

1) Do you need the entire evidence folder downloadable in one bundle (zip), or will the auditor be downloading individual files?
2) Can Audit Partners accept SAML/Okta? If not, we'll issue a single-use token tied to an email + IP range.
3) Does Acme require a signed bridge letter for the Apr–Jun 2026 range, or only if some items are archived and cannot be surfaced?

Our recommended path for speed + audit trail:
- Create a one-time, single-use download token scoped to a named bundle (we generate a signed token file and a portal link).
- Token TTL: configurable up to 72 hours; default we suggest 48h per your ask.
- IP allowlist: we can accept CIDR(s) you provide.
- Audit trail: every download is logged and we can produce an export (CSV) showing file, timestamp, and IP.

If you prefer a sponsored reviewer account (view+download), that takes slightly longer (we need an internal provisioning step and an incoming ID verification).

Next steps: send me Oliver's preferred email and IP egress CIDR and confirm "bundle vs individual files." I can create the token and reply with a temporary-token.txt (contains the link + token id) and a portal link (trust.redwood.ai) that your auditor will use.

Attaching: guidance doc (requested_evidence_list.pdf) and a short runbook for token acceptance.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Account Security Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@auditpartners.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, sara.chen@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-18T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived auditor access + download scope for SOC 2 artifacts

Thanks Nikhil, Sara — Oliver here. Per procurement, we cannot onboard to Acme's Okta instance for a short engagement. A single-use download token scoped to the bundle is ideal. Answers below: 

- Preferred email: oliver.park@auditpartners.com
- IP egress: 54.210.0.0/16 (Audit Partners egress range) — please restrict to this if possible.
- We will download the entire "ACME_SOC2_EVIDENCE_2026" bundle as a single zip.

Security notes: we require the token to be single-use (one browser session or programmatic download) and to expire after 48 hours. Please confirm that the token will be logged with a per-file audit record and that Redwood can provide a CSV of the access events after the session.

If there are any forms for us to sign for access, send them over and I'll get them back same day.

—Oliver
Oliver Park
Senior IT Auditor, Audit Partners

—Nikhil
